segments.text: This $250 device is at the center of my $2.6 million female health experiment. And here's why it's changing female [music] science. In typical scientific literature, the menstrual cycle is treated as something to iron out. But our experiment does the opposite. We put my hormones at the center of science.

And every one of my 1900 biomarkers that we're tracking maps back to where my hormones are at daily. Until 1993, women were not required in US clinical trials. Even now, many studies only test women in the first couple of days of their cycle when [music] their hormones are lowest and most maleike. Okay, so what's the problem with that? It [music] misses the female experience. Things like cholesterol swinging by 19% through the month, and estrogen can rise by eight-fold. This at home hormone monitor does readings by urine every morning. We can then compare my biomarkers from my skin to my brain to where I'm at every day with my hormones. This is just one
part of our 14 million data point study. Follow along if you're interested in finding what happens.
